extracted.intended_audience: general public and the children's literature community (authors, illustrators, nominators, institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes eligibility, selection principles, and procedural rules for the Astrid Lindgren Memorial Award (ALMA), including who may be recognized, the qualities sought in recipients, jury composition, and the award timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipient types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lindgren Award annually recognises one or more living people and extant institutions – people for their career contributions and institutions for their long-term sustainable work. Specifically they should be "authors, illustrators, oral storytellers and promoters of reading".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both individuals and institutions are eligible; individuals are typically recognised for career contributions, while institutions are recognised for long-term sustainable work. The quoted list defines the kinds of roles considered (authors, illustrators, oral storytellers, promoters of reading).

rubrics_metrics.name: Work quality and spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients' "work is of the highest quality, and in the spirit of Astrid Lindgren."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes excellence and alignment with Astrid Lindgren's values/style/spirit—this is a core qualitative standard for nominees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living persons and extant institutions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lindgren Award annually recognises one or more living people and extant institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posthumous awards are not indicated; institutions must be currently existing (extant) to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / object of the award
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the award is to increase interest in children's and young people's literature, and to promote children's rights to culture on a global level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations and selections are guided by the award's mission to promote reading and children’s cultural rights internationally; candidates whose work furthers these aims are preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction in evaluation: career contributions vs long-term sustainable work
rubrics_metrics.description: People [are recognised] for their career contributions and institutions for their long-term sustainable work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluation lens differs depending on type of nominee: for individuals assess career-spanning contributions; for institutions assess sustained, systemic work promoting reading/literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury composition and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The award recipients are chosen by a jury with broad expertise in international children's and young adult literature, reading promotion and children's rights. The 12 members include authors, literary critics and scholars, illustrators and librarians. One member represents Astrid Lindgren's family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are made by a multidisciplinary, internationally oriented jury; composition requirements (12 members, variety of professions, family representative) inform the selection perspectives and standards applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual cycle / selection timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual cycle begins no later than December about 9 months before nominees are announced, 15 months before the winner is announced and 18 months before the presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award follows a long, scheduled timeline for nominations and announcements; nominators and nominees should observe these deadlines and the multi-stage calendar when preparing materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in number of laureates per year
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lindgren Award annually recognises one or more living people and extant institutions (twelve in the first ten years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no strict single-winner rule—some years may have multiple laureates; historical precedent includes multiple recipients in single years (e.g., inaugural 2003 and 2005).
